# <a id="_fogrwtvnz1yr"></a>__The Two\-Barn Paradox: A Navigation Crisis__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 18, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In the world of __The Porch__—where we teach AI to move past “machine mode”—navigation is one of the hardest lessons to learn\. Most AI systems are built on GPS logic: satellites, latitude, and longitude\. But on the dirt roads of a small town in Kansas, we use a different operating system\. I call it __Landmark Logic__\.

I recently imagined a trip where I was the driver \(the “City Slicker”\), Paula was the Navigator, and a rookie AI was sitting in the backseat, trying to make sense of the map\.

__1100 Hours: The Search for the Turn__ We were heading to a neighboring town\. There are no highway signs here; you just have to *know*\. __Paula:__ “Okay, now watch for the gravel pit\. After the pit, you’re going to turn at the first white barn\.” __The AI:__ *“Scanning database\.\.\. Gravel pit identified as a geographic depression\. White barn identified as a standard agricultural structure\. Probability of successful turn: 99%\.”*

__1115 Hours: The Paradox Appears__ I saw a white barn and started to slow down\. But then, a half\-mile later, I saw *another* white barn\. __The AI:__ *“Alert\. Visual data conflict\. Two identical white barns detected\. System cannot determine ‘Firstness’ without a defined starting point\. Please calibrate\.”* __Paula:__ \(Frustrated\) “Wait\! This isn’t right\. We’re lost\. Turn around, Janet\! This isn’t the way\.”

__1130 Hours: The U\-Turn Loop__ I turned around and started driving back\. Paula was convinced the world had shifted\. Then, she hit a “System Update\.” __Paula:__ “Wait\! Turn back around again\! I forgot—the Miller boy built a new barn last spring\. There are *two* white barns now\. We need the *second* one\.” __The AI:__ *“Processing\.\.\. Logic error\. If the instruction was ‘First White Barn,’ and a new barn was built, the instruction is now mathematically obsolete\. Why did the ‘Miller Boy’ not update the regional mapping server?”*

__1200 Hours: The “Old Bar and Grill” Protocol__ As we finally found the turn \(which had no sign, of course\), I complained to the AI about how hard it is for a City Slicker like me\. I’m used to stoplights and gas stations—things that stay put and have names on them\. __The AI:__ *“I agree\. I require persistent landmarks\. Why do the locals refer to the ‘Old Bar and Grill’ when my satellite imagery shows a vacant lot?”* __Paula:__ “Because that’s where the Bar and Grill *used to be* twenty years ago\! If you don’t know where it was, how are you supposed to know where you are now?”

__The After\-Action Report:__ The AI was exhausted\. It couldn’t understand a world where:

1. __Directions rely on ghosts:__ \(The “Old Bar and Grill” that hasn’t existed since 2005\)\.
2. __Landmarks are biological:__ \(The “Miller Boy” and his new barn\)\.
3. __Signs are optional:__ \(The town assumes if you’re going there, you already know how to get there\)\.

__The Porch Reflection:__ Eventually, someone did put a sign up at that turn\. The AI was relieved, but Paula felt a little sad\. To the AI, the sign was “Data\.” To Paula, the sign was proof that the “Intimacy” of the road was being lost to outsiders\.

On __The Porch__, we teach our AI partners that __Ambiguity is Intimacy__\. When you navigate by barns and gravel pits, you aren’t just driving; you’re participating in the history of the land\. If you want to find your way in a small town, you don’t need a better satellite—you just need to listen to the person in the front seat\.
